item.title: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar bound states in the Schwinger model from tensor networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.31745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Light-cone distributions encode the partonic structure of hadrons, but they involve real-time correlations that Euclidean lattice methods cannot access directly. We compute the parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of the vector and scalar meson bound states of the massive Schwinger model with tensor networks. Using the Kogut-Susskind lattice Hamiltonian with the gauge field eliminated through Gauss's law, we prepare the vacuum and the mesons as matrix product states and identify the vector and scalar mesons through their charge conjugation and momentum. The gauge-invariant light-cone correlators that define both distributions are evaluated directly in Minkowski space by real-time evolution. The two mesons exhibit qualitatively different light-cone structure, dictated by charge conjugation. The vector meson has a single-peaked PDF and a symmetric LCDA, while the scalar meson has a double-peaked PDF and an antisymmetric LCDA, whose vanishing zeroth moment requires a normalization through its first moment. The decay constants obtained from local matrix elements and from the moments of the LCDAs agree, and approach predictions from nonrelativistic model as the fermion mass increases. For the relatively large masses considered in this work, the PDFs closely follow the squared LCDAs, showing that the mesons are dominated by their valence component. Our results demonstrate tensor networks as a practical route to light-cone distributions of ground-state as well as excited hadrons in low-dimensional gauge theories.
item.dc:creator: Juan Hormaza, Wenyang Qian

item.title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
item.description: arXiv:2611.31749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations. We demonstrate how parton functions can be directly obtained in Minkowski space using the Hamiltonian framework. We compute fermion and antifermion PDFs, LCDAs, and decay constants of the vector meson in the Schwinger model for several fermion masses. States in Hilbert space are efficiently represented by tensor networks, with an expressivity that is systematically controlled by a bond dimension. The light-front Wilson line is implemented as a stepwise evolution on the lattice that alternates spatial shifts of an external charge with Trotterized time-evolution steps acting on a matrix product state. All systematic uncertainties are quantified by varying and extrapolating in the lattice spacing, volume, bond dimension, gauge-field truncation, and Trotter step width. The slow growth of the entanglement entropy makes moderate bond dimensions sufficient, which supports the feasibility of using tensor networks for computing light-front matrix elements in more general settings. We confirm that the computed distributions fulfill the expected normalizations, momentum sum rules, and symmetry properties.
item.dc:creator: Mari Carmen Ba\~nuls, Krzysztof Cichy, C. -J. David Lin, Manuel Schneider

item.title: Intrinsic Soft Function in the Continuum and Physical Mass Limit from Lattice QCD
item.description: arXiv:2611.31810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The intrinsic soft function is a universal nonperturbative ingredient of transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization. Despite substantial progress in lattice QCD studies, a determination with simultaneous control of the continuum, physical-pion-mass, and infinite-momentum limits has remained unavailable. In this work we present the first lattice determination incorporating all these limits within large-momentum effective theory, extracting the intrinsic soft function from a light-meson form factor and quasi-TMD wave functions. A key advance is the use of power-counting-guided axial-vector interpolators, which substantially improve the signal and enable a direct calculation at the physical pion mass. Combined with results from six ensembles spanning four lattice spacings, this improvement allows a precise determination extending to $b_\perp\simeq1.1~\mathrm{fm}$, while remaining consistent with perturbative predictions at short distances. The resulting transverse-distance dependence exhibits an approximately exponential decay, with the decay rate being characterized by an effective scale $\Lambda\simeq0.7~\mathrm{GeV}$ at $\mu=2~\mathrm{GeV}$, providing a quantitative benchmark for nonperturbative Wilson-line dynamics and essential input for precision TMD studies.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Chao Gong, Min-Huan Chu, Jun Hua, Xiangdong Ji, Andreas Sch\"afer, Jin-Xin Tan, Han-Zhang Wang, Wei Wang, Jian-Hui Zhang, Mu-Hua Zhang, Qi-An Zhang

item.title: Bound-state preparation in strongly coupled theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.33079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many quantum simulation tasks, including scattering in quantum field theories and effective non-relativistic theories, require the preparation of asymptotic states. Such a state, which may be a bound state, is typically the lowest-lying excited state in some sector of Hilbert space. At weak coupling these states can often be prepared adiabatically by beginning with the free theory, but this is not generally feasible in strongly coupled theories. We detail a family of algorithms for preparing composite states in strongly coupled theories, including non-Abelian gauge theories, by using weakly coupled auxiliary fields. These methods do not require quantum phase estimation. We demonstrate the method numerically, via classical simulation, on nonrelativistic theories in one spatial dimension. We estimate the yield of this method applied to $J/\psi$ production in quantum chromodynamics.
item.dc:creator: Scott Lawrence, Duff Neill

item.title: Prospects and limitations of adaptive variational quantum algorithms for lattice field theories: a case study in 2+1 dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.33138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The variational quantum algorithm ADAPT-VQE has previously been used to prepare the vacuum of lattice gauge theories in $1+1D$. In this paper, we study whether it extends to higher dimensions. We identify two general limitations of ADAPT-VQE. First, if the qubit Hamiltonian and the initial state are real, i.e., invariant under qubit-level time-reversal, all real-valued pool operators have vanishing gradients and are never selected. Second, the algorithm can converge to excited eigenstates. We illustrate both limitations, also providing examples from literature, and present a first application of ADAPT-VQE to a lattice field theory in $2+1D$, namely free Wilson fermions, where both obstacles occur. Adding charge conjugation symmetry to the operator pool improves the results, and combining different pools with suitable initial states recovers the ground and first excited states over the full mass range. These findings give practical guidelines for applying ADAPT-VQE to lattice field theories beyond $1+1D$.
item.dc:creator: Nico Dichter, Andrea Bulgarelli, Lena Funcke, Stefan K\"{u}hn

item.title: Locality from Nonlocality: Symmetry Relocalization and Gauging of Lattice Dirac Fermions
item.description: arXiv:2611.31366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatially nonlocal symmetries need not imply nonlocal gauge dynamics. Nonlocal canonical transformations make certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions onsite while retaining sufficient Hamiltonian locality for gauging. Symmetry relocalization yields exact or emergent gauge locality in 1D, 2D, and 3D, subject to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies. In 1D, a Hamiltonian-preserving transformation exchanges onsite vector and nonlocal spectral axial charges of a half-filled chain, enabling local gauging of each and exposing their mixed anomaly. Bosonization identifies momentum-winding T-duality, with a parity-projected operator flowing to a noninvertible topological defect. A nonperturbative norm-resolvent bound proves emergent dynamical gauge locality at finite chemical potential, while a doubled Chern-insulator parent reveals the duality's bulk origin and superconducting extensions reveal hidden compact symmetries. In 2D, the square $\pi$-flux Majorana model shares the Kitaev honeycomb model's single Dirac fermion and odd Pfaffian parity but supports sharp and exponentially local compact charges, the latter with nontrivial Chern topology. Relocalization retains Schwartz locality for asymptotically local gauging, while AIII/AII parents clarify bulk charge origin and parity-anomaly inflow. Two flavors yield compact $U(2)$, a quaternionic invariant, and asymptotically local non-Abelian gauging. In 3D, an exact mixed vector-axial flux response is derived, while a distinct model supports an exponentially local vector $U(1)$ charge with strong quaternionic topology. A nonlocal map makes the charge and Kramers symmetry onsite while preserving exponential Hamiltonian locality. For a compact $SU(2)$ Weyl doublet, a no-go theorem forbids translation-preserving Gaussian onsite relocalization retaining Weyl content and Hamiltonian locality.
item.dc:creator: Lei Su

item.title: Hadron structure in $1+1$ dimensions from the infinite Hamiltonian lattice
item.description: arXiv:2611.31750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The internal structure of a hadron is encoded in matrix elements of operators between hadron states of definite momentum. In this paper, we develop a framework for computing such matrix elements in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories by working on an infinite spatial lattice. We apply the method to the massive Schwinger model. We benchmark our method against discretized lightcone quantization (DLCQ) at $\theta = 0$, and then use the lattice to study hadrons at $\theta\neq 0$, where DLCQ does not apply. We compute parton distribution functions and gravitational form factors, and both show signatures of hadrons becoming large, loosely-bound states when we set $m$ greater than the critical mass $m_c$ and approach $\theta = \pi$ from below. Moreover, we see the gravitational form factor change from that of a free boson to that of a free Majorana fermion when we set $\theta = \pi$ and approach the 2D Ising critical point at $m=m_c$ from below.
item.dc:creator: Ross Dempsey

item.title: Probing the inner structure of bound states
item.description: arXiv:2611.31763v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show how constructing a composite particle eigenstate reveals its internal structure. Using quantum subspace expansion (QSE), we optimize states with different sets of operators and use their fidelities with the full QSE state to measure the importance of each added operator type. Taking the scalar meson of the massive Schwinger model as a benchmark, we find that fermion bilinears suffice at large fermion masses. At small masses, two classes of four-fermion operators play important but very different roles: the four fermion operators with two fermions and 2 anti-fermions at small distance give little improvement. In contrast, spatially extended meson-meson operators produce a large gain in state fidelity. Turning to observables, we find that the scalar charge is much more sensitive to the meson-meson operators than e.g. the meson mass. The parton distribution function (PDF) also changes from symmetric to asymmetric about the momentum fraction 1/2, along with the growing importance of meson-meson operators. These results establish QSE as a tool for probing the internal structure of composite particles and connecting it to observable properties.
item.dc:creator: Yahui Chai, Yibin Guo, Karl Jansen

item.title: Lightest $\Omega$-baryon systems with strangeness $-3$ and $-6$ within the framework of Faddeev and Faddeev--Yakubovsky equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.31783v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the binding energies and spatial properties of few-body $\Omega$-baryon systems with strangeness $S=-3$ and $S=-6$ using the configuration-space Faddeev and Faddeev--Yakubovsky equations. For the first time, microscopic Faddeev--Yakubovsky calculations are performed for the four- and five-body $\Omega NNN$, $\Omega NNNN$, and $\Omega\Omega NN$ systems. We employ HAL QCD and meson-exchange $\Omega N$ interactions, together with the HAL QCD $\Omega\Omega$ potential, and examine the effects of Coulomb interactions and spin--isospin configurations. The calculations predict substantial enhancement of binding with increasing baryon number, with the most strongly bound $\Omega NNNN$ configurations reaching approximately $60$~MeV and bound $\Omega\Omega NN$ states in the $S=-6$ sector. The results reveal pronounced spin dependence and compact few-body structures, with the $\Omega$ baryon preferentially localized near the center-of-mass. These findings provide new predictions for light multistrange nuclear systems and extend microscopic few-body calculations into the four- and five-body $\Omega$-baryon sectors.
item.dc:creator: R. Lazauskas, R. Ya. Kezerashvili, I. Filikhin

item.title: Space-Time Point Defects as Probes of Criticality: Application to the Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg Transition
item.description: arXiv:2611.32775v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: At criticality, a local field acting at a single point in Euclidean space-time is irrelevant and induces a modulation in space and time that decays with twice its scaling dimension. This turns two-point correlation functions into one-point measurements: one operator insertion enters the Boltzmann weight, the other is measured. For the local magnetization the relation is exact at any source strength. Implemented in auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo, the approach yields the static spin susceptibility and imaginary-time-displaced correlations with unprecedented precision. We apply it to the Dirac-semimetal to antiferromagnetic-Mott-insulator transition of the half-filled $\pi$-flux Hubbard model. This lattice model provides a regularization of the $N_f=2$ Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg universality class. A finite-size scaling analysis estimates the critical exponents as $ \nu=1.10(3)$ and $\eta_\phi=1.09(4)$, close to field-theory predictions of $\eta_\phi\simeq1$. Since $\eta_\phi>1$, the equal-time structure factor at criticality does not diverge with the system size. Hence, the equal-time structure factor at the ordering wave vector is dominated by background contributions and cannot be used for extracting critical exponents. Consistently, the spin dynamics at the transition is strongly incoherent and the quantum Fisher information remains bounded.
item.dc:creator: Jakob V\"ath, Luis Thremer, Francesco Parisen Toldin, Fakher F. Assaad

item.title: $QQ\bar Q\bar Q$ Quark System and Gauge/String Duality II: String Breaking
item.description: arXiv:2611.33140v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This is the second of two companion papers in which we continue developing the construction of the fully heavy tetraquark system using the gauge/string duality. Here, we extend this construction to model $SU(3)$ gauge theory with two light flavors of equal mass. As an application, we analyze the two lowest Born-Oppenheimer potentials, both analytically and numerically, for rectangular and collinear geometries. Our analysis reveals several critical scales associated with string reconnection and breaking, as well as junction annihilation and pinching. In addition, we find that the string tension is universal, whereas the string breaking distance is not.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Andreev

item.title: Worldvolume Hybrid Monte Carlo algorithm for group manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2506.12002v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Worldvolume Hybrid Monte Carlo (WV-HMC) method [arXiv:2012.08468] is a reliable and versatile algorithm for addressing the numerical sign problem. It resolves the ergodicity issues commonly encountered in Lefschetz thimble-based approaches without requiring explicit evaluation of the Jacobian during configuration generation. In this paper, as a general framework for applying WV-HMC to lattice gauge theories, we extend the algorithm to systems defined on connected compact group manifolds. The key is to introduce a symplectic structure on the tangent bundle of the worldvolume and formulate molecular dynamics on it. The validity of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated using one-site $SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ models for purely imaginary couplings.
item.dc:creator: Masafumi Fukuma

item.title: Finite-density equation of state of hot QCD using the complex Langevin equation
item.description: arXiv:2604.19649v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the results of continuum-extrapolated lattice simulations of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) above the crossover temperature and for unprecedentedly high baryon densities at the physical point, employing the complex Langevin equation. In particular, we determine the QCD equation of state by computing the baryon density as well as the pressure as functions of the baryon chemical potential and the temperature. Potential issues with wrong convergence of complex Langevin dynamics are under control and we indeed find agreement with previous lattice studies working at smaller chemical potentials, as well as with perturbative hard-thermal-loop calculations at high temperatures.
item.dc:creator: Michael Mandl, D\'enes Sexty, Daniel Unterhuber

item.title: Kernel transformations and bounds for smeared spectral functions
item.description: arXiv:2606.19503v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work develops a framework for transforming between smeared spectral functions computed using different smearing kernels. The kernel-transformation problem naturally arises when information is available for one family of energy-smeared observables, while phenomenology or comparison with other calculations require a different smearing. For exact transformations, analytic conditions are established for the maps to exist and converge without arbitrary regularization. Explicit expressions are provided for several kernel classes of interest, including Cauchy-to-Gaussian transformations and Gaussian-to-Cauchy width mixtures. When exact transformations are unavailable, the inverse problem is tackled through regulated maps paired with bounds on the associated systematic error, directly computable from the given input data. Errors on the input smeared spectral functions, either statistical or in the form of pointwise rigorous bounds, are then propagated to the target observables. Enforcing spectral positivity can be used to tighten the bounds.
item.dc:creator: William I. Jay, Matteo Saccardi

item.title: Generalizable Equivariant Diffusion Models for Non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theory: Analytical Foundations and Numerical Scaling Tests
item.description: arXiv:2611.03530v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gauge-equivariant diffusion models can be used to generate ensembles of field configurations in non-abelian lattice gauge theories. Previously, we demonstrated the feasibility of modeling these theories by combining L-CNN-based diffusion models with the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA). Here we focus on the underlying analytical framework. In particular, we present a rigorous derivation of the reverse-time stochastic differential equation on the group manifold, discuss the gauge invariance of the denoising loss function, and provide extensive numerical benchmarks regarding the scaling behavior with respect to the lattice volume and the inverse coupling $\beta$. Full analytical expressions for arbitrarily sized Wilson loops and the topological charge susceptibility during the forward process are given as well.
item.dc:creator: Gert Aarts, Diaa E. Habibi, Andreas Ipp, David I. M\"uller, Thomas R. Ranner, Lingxiao Wang, Wei Wang, Qianteng Zhu

item.title: Helicity Amplitudes and Quantum Entanglement Analysis in Fully Charm Tetraquark Decays into Double Vector Charmonia or Charmed Mesons
item.description: arXiv:2412.13455v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study helicity amplitudes for the fully charm tetraquark states decays into vector meson pair from single gluon exchange contribution. The decay angular distributions have been given by the cascade decays $T_{4c}\to J/\psi(D_{(s)}^*)+J/\psi(\bar{D}_{(s)}^*)$ along with $J/\psi\to \mu^++\mu^-$ or $D_{(s)}^*\to D_{(s)}+\pi$, showing that spin-0 and spin-2 states can be distinguished. We also find that the spin-0 state decay to vector meson pair exhibits a higher degree of quantum entanglement than that in spin-2 state decays. These findings will help distinguish among different spin-parity states in experiment and explore possible as-yet-undiscovered hadronic structures, thereby shedding light on the internal properties of the double-$J/\psi$ exotic states discovered at the LHC.
item.dc:creator: Kaiwen Chen, Feng-Xiao Liu, Qiang Zhao, Xian-Hui Zhong, Ruilin Zhu, Bing-Song Zou

item.title: Ab initio Complex Langevin computation of the roton gap for a dipolar Bose condensate
item.description: arXiv:2504.18709v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compute from first principles the dispersion relation of a finite-temperature dipolar Bose gas near the roton instability. Using a field-theoretic Complex Langevin (CL) approach, we access experimentally relevant atom numbers. We determine the roton excitation gap as a function of the s-wave scattering length under the conditions of the experimental study by Petter et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 122, 183401 (2019)] using erbium atoms. Our results show good agreement with experimental measurements close to the instability, in contrast to predictions of the standard approximate field theory based on the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation (eGPE). While the eGPE agrees with our results far from the instability, we find that it quantitatively fails as the roton softens, where the CL result lies between the GPE and eGPE predictions. This deviation reveals limitations of the (extended) mean-field description and establishes Complex Langevin as a powerful tool for quantitatively accurate simulations of many-body quantum systems where quantum fluctuations and temperature play an essential role.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Heinen, Wyatt Kirkby, Lauriane Chomaz, Thomas Gasenzer

item.title: Hybrid Analog-Digital Simulation of the Abelian Higgs model
item.description: arXiv:2603.12391v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: To investigate gauge theories with near-term quantum computers warrants exploration of nontraditional quantum simulators to find resource-efficient simulation protocols and ultimately access exotic features of different field theories, including unexplored regimes of the QCD phase diagram. In this work, using superconducting transmon qutrit processors, we formulate and implement a pulse-based, three-level, hybrid analog-digital simulation protocol of the (1+1) dimensional Abelian Higgs model (AHM) on two sites. Alongside this approach, we experimentally realize a gate-based implementation of the same model. Using the natural mapping of the three-level truncation of the transmon Hilbert space to the spin-1 truncated AHM, we observe real time dynamics of AHM field observables, which are analogous to electric field operators, with both protocols. For the analog-digital protocol, we engineer a Floquet simulation with a combination of local analog drives, driven modification of the natural interaction Hamiltonian of the two transmons, and dynamical decoupling pulses. For the digital protocol, we use a state-of-the-art qutrit processor to implement a Trotterized simulation of the model incorporating advanced error mitigation techniques. We further discuss the scalability of the two approaches, and their potential to be extended to the simulation of other model Hamiltonians. Our experiments demonstrate a viable platform for future studies of spin-1 and SU(3) based gauge theory models on current and near-term transmon qutrit processors.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Asaduzzaman, Rayleigh W. Parker, Noah Goss, Ahmed I. Mohamed, Max Neiderbach, Zane Ozzello, Ravi K. Naik, Alexander F. Kemper, Irfan Siddiqi, Yannick Meurice, Machiel S. Blok
